data.title: Lockheed Martin wins $1.53B contract boost for Trident II missile work
data.description:
• Lockheed Martin (LMT) received an unpriced letter contract modification with a not-to-exceed value of $1.53B for TRIDENT II (D5) missile production and deployed systems support.
  • The work will be performed across multiple U.S. locations, with expected completion by September 30, 2031.  
  • The Strategic Systems Program is the contracting activity.

data.title: AI coding platform Cognition embarks on new $2B funding round: report
data.description:
Cognition AI, which offers an AI-powered coding and engineering platform, has entered talks for a new $2B funding round, which would elevate the startup to a $75B valuation, according to Bloomberg.

The company's primary products compete with Anthropic's (ANT) Claude Code, OpenAI's (OPENAI) Codex and SpaceX's (SPCX) Cursor, to name a few.

The San Francisco-based company has already raised more than $3B this year in other funding rounds, according to the report. Some of Cognition's clients include Wayfair (W), Cititgroup (C), and Mercedez-Benz (MBGAF). The company recently said it was on track to reach $1B in annualized revenue by the end of the year, which is double from four months ago.

data.title: Melar Acquisition changes name to Everli Global Holdings
data.description:
•  Melar Acquisition (MACI) said on Friday that it changed its name to Everli Global Holdings following the completion of a business combination with Everli.
  • The Nasdaq Stock Market has approved the listing of Everli's Class A common stock and warrants on the Nasdaq Global Market, where they are expected to begin trading on November 23, 2026, under the ticker symbols "EVRL" and "EVRLW," respectively.
  • Press Release

data.title: Bayer’s $7.25B Roundup settlement approved by U.S. judge
data.description:
A Missouri judge on Friday approved Bayer's (BAYRY) (BAYZF) $7.25B settlement of lawsuits alleging its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer, which could help pave the way toward resolving litigation that ​has weighed on the company for a decade.

The agreement is "fair, reasonable, and adequate" and serves "the best interests of the class representatives," the Missouri Circuit Court judge said in his ruling approving the proposal.

Roundup litigation has posed a major headache for Bayer (BAYRY) (BAYZF), which inherited the legal troubles with its purchase of Monsanto in 2018; the shares tanked 80% in the years after the acquisition, although recent legal wins have helped recover some of the losses.

Bayer's (BAYRY) (BAYZF) settlement, announced in February, aims to resolve nearly all current and future Roundup ​claims in the U.S.

When Bayer (BAYRY) (BAYZF) unveiled the settlement, it was still awaiting a U.S. Supreme Court ruling on whether it could be sued over its government-approved warning label for Roundup; the company ultimately won the case, undercutting a ​central claim in many ​of the lawsuits against it.

The proposed settlement offers payouts ranging from $10K to $165K to ​people who were exposed to Roundup and developed non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with the ​exact award depending on the severity of their cancer, their age, and whether they were an occupational or residential user of Roundup.

data.title: Twenty One Capital adds $10M in Bitcoin, holdings reach 43,841 BTC
data.description:
• Twenty One Capital (XXI) purchased 172.25 Bitcoin for $10M, at an average price of ~$58,054 per BTC, using cash.

  • The latest purchase brings the company's total Bitcoin holdings to ~43,841 BTC as of November 20, 2026.

  • The company has purchased a combined 326.57 BTC for $20 M across two announcements this week, including its November 16 purchase of 154.32 BTC.

data.title: GM's CEO succession plan could include tech-savvy executive -- Bloomberg
data.description:
The search for a successor to Mary Barra at General Motors (GM) could focus on someone with technical expertise and deep knowledge of self-driving technology, putting GM’s chief product officer Sterling Anderson as a top contender for the chief executive job.

According to Bloomberg, Anderson has met with board members for one-on-one meetings, although the purpose of these meetings is unconfirmed.

The company has reportedly begun searching for Barra’s successor, preparing for whenever she steps down from the role she has held since 2014. 

While GM’s (GM) recent move to the Nasdaq exchange means the company is no longer mandated to have a succession plan, the GM board is aware that as Barra approaches her 65th birthday on December 24, the time has come to have her replacement in place.

According to Bloomberg, Anderson is the frontrunner, but the company is also reportedly considering CFO Paul Jacobson and GM President Mark Reuss, as well as outside candidates recommended by executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles.

data.title: Theriva Biologics sets 1-for-30 reverse split; stock crashes after-hours
data.description:
• Theriva Biologics (TOVX) announced on Friday a 1-for-30 reverse stock split, effective December 1, 2026, after market close.
  • The shares will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis on December 2.
  • The reverse split aims to help the company meet NYSE American's minimum share price requirement.
  • The split will reduce outstanding shares from approximately 45.9M to 1.53M, while proportionally reducing authorized shares.
  • Meanwhile, the company will continue trading under the same ticker, with a new CUSIP number.
  • However, on the market side, the stock crashed over 16% to ~$0.10 in the after-hours trading session.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: The Marketing Alliance authorizes repurchase of up to 800,000 shares
data.description:
The Marketing Alliance (MAAL) announced Friday the company's board of directors has authorized a share repurchase program to repurchase up to 800,000 shares of the company's issued and outstanding common stock, effective immediately and concluding March 31, 2027.

Timothy Klusas, the company's president and chief executive officer, stated, "The Board continues to believe that share repurchases are a superior way to reward shareholders. In the past, the Board felt its policy of paying dividends was not adequately reflected in the stock price.”

Source: press release

data.title: Oatly gets $4.13 per ADS cash tender offer from shareholder Verlinvest
data.description:
• Oatly Group (OTLY) announced on Friday that Verlinvest had launched a cash tender offer for all outstanding shares at $0.2065 per ordinary share, or $4.13 per ADS.

  • Verlinvest said the offer was a technical requirement under Swedish law related to its proposed buyout of China Resources' indirect stake in Oatly.

  • Oatly's independent directors are reviewing the offer and will issue a formal recommendation to shareholders by December 4, 2026.

  • The company urged shareholders not to take action until the board issues its recommendation.

data.title: Insulet downgraded at Baird on concerns over insulin pump loyalty
data.description:
• Baird downgraded Insulet (PODD) to Neutral from Overweight, citing a recent survey that found lower brand loyalty to automated insulin delivery (AID) systems than in the past. 
  • The firm cut its price target to $158 from $200 (~19% upside based on Friday's close).
  • Analyst Jeff Johnson said that Seagrove Partners' 2026 Patient Perspectives report of more than 700 people with diabetes found that individuals with an Insulet AID system had less brand loyalty than those using other companies' systems.
  • "With this lower brand loyalty, willingness to switch to alternate AID systems next year also grew, with even current Omnipod wearers voicing greater willingness than we expected to potentially switch to a competing AID system next year."
  • Johnson warned that the findings could benefit Insulet's rivals, as "only [Tandem Diabetes Care's (TNDM)] Mobi Tubeless and [MiniMed's (MMED)] Fit check both these 'tighter algo' and '7-day wear potential' boxes, with Mobi-T fitting this latter point better than Fit, in our view."
